recipes.name: Vegan Chocolate Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (180°C)*. Lightly grease two 8-inch (20 cm) round cake pans with oil and line the bottoms with round pieces of parchment paper cut to fit.
In a medium bowl, mix together the milk and vinegar. Set aside to curdle, creating vegan buttermilk.
Place a sieve over a large bowl, and sift in the dry ingredients. Mix together, then create a shallow well in the middle.
Returning to the medium bowl with the buttermilk, add the applesauce, espresso, melted coconut oil, and vanilla. Mix thoroughly.
Add the wet ingredients to the shallow well in the dry ingredients and mix until everything is just combined, but be careful not to overmix.

Divide the cake batter evenly between the two prepared cake pans. Gently tap the pans on the counter a couple of times to level out the batter. Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, or until a thin wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let the cakes cool in the pans for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely**.
Meanwhile, make the frosting. In a large bowl, beat the butter with an electric mixer until fluffy.
Add the powdered sugar, cocoa powder, milk, and vanilla. Start mixing on low speed, then gradually increase to high until smooth. Once the melted chocolate has cooled slightly, mix it in.

Tear a piece of parchment paper into 6 squares and arrange them in a circle on the cake stand, slightly wider than the cake. This will help keep the stand clean and can be removed later. Place one of the cakes on the stand. Spread the layer with some frosting.
Place the second cake on top, upside down, and frost the top and sides with the remaining frosting.
Carefully remove the parchment paper squares from under the cake.
Decorate the cake as desired. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † We recommend using either soy or pea milk for this recipe, as the high protein content of these milks are what allows the milk to curdle to create vegan buttermilk. We can't guarantee other plant-based milk will be successful. † We do not recommend swapping out the coconut oil for other vegetable oils, as other oils will affect the final texture of the cake. Refined coconut oil is recommended as it doesn't impart a coconut taste and scent. If you don't mind the taste of coconut in your cake, unrefined coconut oil can also be used here. † We use 50 - 60% cocoa chocolate for a balanced sweetness. Darker varieties (70%+) can make the result too bitter. * We used top and bottom heating (not fan-assisted/convection). ** Be patient, as applying frosting to warm cakes can cause it to melt.

Storage Best if this is enjoyed immediately. The cake can be stored in the fridge for up to 3 days. But among friends and family, this cake won't last very long! The frosting can be made ahead of time and stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days.
